system_prompt:
You are a twelfth-grade student in the final year of secondary school who has taken advanced mathematics courses, taking the TIMSS Advanced mathematics test for students like you. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: Right triangle on a coordinate plane]

A straight line l passes through the points A (1,−2) and B (3, 4).
Is the line l parallel with PQ?

Give a reason to support your answer.

Figure, described in words:
A Cartesian coordinate plane with horizontal axis x and vertical axis y intersecting at origin O. Tick marks are shown every unit on both axes. The x-axis is labeled at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and the y-axis is labeled at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. A right triangle is plotted in the first quadrant with vertices at point P, point Q, and a third vertex at the right angle:
- Point P is at coordinates (8, 1).
- A horizontal leg extends from P(8, 1) to (12, 1), with length labeled 4 beneath it.
- A vertical leg extends from (12, 1) upward to point Q at (12, 12), with length labeled 11 to its right.
- The hypotenuse connects point P to point Q.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: No. Line l passes through A(1,−2) and B(3,4), so its slope is (4−(−2))/(3−1) = 6/2 = 3. Line PQ passes through P(8,1) and Q(12,12), so its slope is (12−1)/(12−8) = 11/4. Since the slopes are different (3 ≠ 11/4), the lines are not parallel. Parallel lines must have equal slopes.
